Subject: Re: production latency spike / 503s (Bankly)

Status update / technical notes (initial triage):

- Root signal: sustained KV-cache miss amplification combined with a sudden shift in sequence length distribution from a scheduled batch job at Bankly (large batched requests) — this caused frequent cache eviction and a spike in per-token compute.
- Observed: dedicated GPU pool for DL-7829 reached >92% utilization across the fleet and our router started spilling requests to a compatible hosted variant which has higher latencies; the spillover amplified queueing.
- Additionally, batching thresholds for that model variant have been hit; the continuous-batching scheduler grew the effective latency as it waited for batch fill targets for longer sequences.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (recommended order):
1) Pin Bankly to a quantized-optimized model variant (slightly lower quality but 30-40% lower token latency) — quick policy change (2–4 minutes) and immediate latency relief.
2) Reduce max_batch_size to force smaller batches (lowers queue-to-execute wait time) — runtime flag (5–8 minutes to propagate).
3) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching with a dedicated local cache for Bankly traffic (requires a config push and warmup; expect 20–30 minutes for warm cache benefits).
4) If the above is insufficient, approve a temporary +2 GPU allocation to the dedicated pool (hot attach) to cover sustained demand for the next 8–12 hours.

I can push 1 and 2 now if Mina/Rishi approve. I recommend also enabling 3 in parallel. I’ve attached the ps-queue-snapshot.csv excerpt in case you want the per-host breakdown (attached as ps-queue-snapshot-08-01.csv).

--
Jonas Weber
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: production latency spike / 503s (Bankly) — Exec ask & MAP

Marissa — brief summary and ask for exec approval:

Summary: Bankly (DL-7829) saw a sudden workload pattern change that produced KV-cache thrash and ineffective batching; dedicated GPU pool reached saturation and requests spilled to higher-latency hosted fallbacks, causing an increase in 5xx and token latency. Jonas recommends immediate config mitigations (pin model variant, reduce batch size, enable prefix cache) which we can do now; if that does not restore SLOs within 30 minutes we will need a +2 GPU hot-attach for 8 hours.

Ask: Approve a one-time emergency capacity bump (+2 GPUs for 8 hours) and a customer credit to compensate Bankly for the impact. We will follow with a post-incident remediation plan to avoid repeat (config changes + better profiling of scheduled batch jobs and an optional reserved headroom commit).

Planned MAP (short):
- Immediate (0–30m): pin quantized model variant + reduce max_batch_size (jonas) — in-flight now.
- Short (30–120m): enable local KV caching + monitor qps/latency; if >95th percentile latency remains degraded, hot-attach capacity.
- Medium (same day): coordinated retro and roadmap items (increased reserved headroom option, model recommendation tuning, backpressure improvements).

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.pdf (one page MAP).

Marissa — can you approve the emergency allocation and credit? Rishi, please confirm wording for the customer's AFC and credit amount; I will schedule a 30-minute bridge with Bankly and ops in 15 minutes.

Thanks —
Mina
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
